reason: The text features multiple regular human characters who demonstrate clear agency through deliberate actions and decisions. The Israelite people actively make requests of Aaron (ק֣וּם עֲשֵׂה־ לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים), voluntarily remove their golden earrings (וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ כָּל־ הָעָם אֶת־ נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב), and collectively decide to worship the calf (וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־ לוֹ וַיִּזְבְּחוּ). Aaron chooses to craft the calf (וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל) and build an altar. Moses demonstrates agency by ascending the mountain, reporting between God and people, breaking the tablets when angry, and interceding for the people. Joshua also exhibits agency by hearing and reporting what he perceives. These are all human characters making intentional choices that drive the narrative.
